title: Henk audit record
description: One record per EVENT TRIAGE (written at triage completion), per owner session, per suppressed event, per MUTATION AUTHORIZATION (written at decision time), or per REMINDER LIFECYCLE TRANSITION (written after the store transaction commits). Schema version 5 adds four optional, nullable fields to the session record: `profile`, `effort`, `recording_id` and `prior_handoff_ids`. It documents the session `outcome` values and rewrites the description of `memory_hash`, because an event-triage record now carries a non-null hash when the triage received recall. Version 5 renames, retypes and re-means no version-4 field, so a reader of version-4 records reads version-5 records correctly. Version 4 added: the `reminder` record type and the `scheduler` value for `initiated_by`, declaring the COMPLETE transition enumeration for the reminder capability, including the transitions only the delivery half writes — a schema document is a validation contract, not an inventory of what the current build emits. Version 3 added: the `authorization` record type (model-initiated decisions and owner-command receipts), the tier+outcome shape of session `approvals` entries (v2 used `decision`), the `executed` flag on `tool_calls` entries, and the session record's `memory_hash`.

at.description: Unix time the record was produced (informational).

event.description: For event-triggered triages: the incidents triaged.

result_id.description: The tool's returned identifier, retained ONLY for tools whose result the application consumes — in practice `publish_handoff`, whose value becomes this record's handoff_message_id. Null for every other tool: results are not recorded, so no tool output (node addresses, note content, stored memories, captured thoughts) enters the audit log.

executed.description: True when the invocation was permitted to proceed. Derived by correlating the invocation with this session's authorization records — never inferred from tool-result text. Read-only and notify-only calls are true by construction: they bypass the gate.

approvals.description: Every mutating-tool authorization decision made during this session. Non-empty whenever a mutating tool was invoked. Owner-command receipts are NOT listed here: commands run outside any turn or session and live only as standalone authorization records.

tier.description: The tool's DECLARED authorization tier (a tool property, so it is reported even when the kill-switch demoted its enforcement).

memory_hash.description: Content hash of the recall block this session received, as injected. For an event-triage record it is the hash of the block that triage's event turn received (event turns receive recall), and an owner continuation inside a triage session inherits it. Null when no block was injected: an empty store, a recall that failed to read, or a session that received no recall. Makes the memory state a session saw auditable.

outcome.description: Session records: how the session's turn ended. `completed`: a reply was produced. `error`: the model or the SDK reported an error, or the turn raised. `refused`: the stop reason was a refusal. `no-reply`: the turn ended without error or refusal but produced no reply text. For any value other than `completed`, the reply text is discarded, not delivered. Documented rather than enumerated, so the field keeps its version-4 type.

cache_read_input_tokens.description: Cache-read input tokens (prompt caching); additive to the uncached input_tokens.

profile.description: Session records: the profile of the session factory that created this session. `event` for an event triage and for an owner continuation inside a triage session; `chat` otherwise. Null when the writer did not name one.

effort.description: Session records: the reasoning effort of the session factory that created this session, as passed to the SDK. Null when the writer did not name one or the CLI default applied.

recording_id.description: Event-triage records: the id of that triage's recording (triage-replay). Null when no recording was written, and on every record that is not an event triage, owner continuations included. A reference, never recording content.

prior_handoff_ids.description: Event-triage records: the row ids, in the local handoff archive, of the retained prior handoffs the triage's digest showed, as an empty list when none were shown. A row id rather than the handoff's published id, because a retained handoff always has a row id and may have no published id. Null on every record that is not an event triage, owner continuations included. References, never handoff text.

tool.description: Authorization records: the named action. A registered tool name for model-initiated decisions; the command itself (e.g. `/forget`) for owner-command receipts.

tier.description: Authorization records: the tool's declared tier. Null for owner commands — a tier is a tool property and a command is not a tool.

initiated_by.description: Authorization and reminder records: who initiated the action. `scheduler` is written only by the reminder-delivery half (every delivered, missed and abandoned transition); it is declared in v4 so delivery needs no new version.

reference.description: Authorization records: the gate's one-time invocation reference. Null for owner commands (no gate involvement — the gate governs model-initiated calls).

turn_type.description: Authorization records: the kind of turn the decision was made in. `command` means it ran outside any turn or session.

detail.description: Authorization records: a bounded summary of the effect (owner commands name what changed, e.g. how many memories were removed). Reminder records: restricted to a closed vocabulary by the reminder branch below — see its description.

reminder_id.description: Reminder records: the reminder's store id.

due_at.description: Reminder records: the reminder's resolved due instant, epoch seconds. The instant rather than a rendered string, because rendering depends on the currently configured zone and a receipt must not move.

transition.description: Reminder records: the name of the LIFECYCLE TRANSITION, not the stored row status — a reinstated reminder's row status is `pending`. The COMPLETE enumeration for the capability: `delivered`, `delivered-late`, `missed` and `abandoned` are written only by the reminder-delivery half and validate here before that half exists.

detail.description: Reminder records: a CLOSED vocabulary, never free text. The only value is 'partial', marking a delivery whose send returned a partial outcome and was recorded as delivered anyway. Constrained by enum rather than by type so this property can never become a route for owner-personal reminder text into the log.
